the_trade_off_made: We favored overall impact and security over pure revenue or strict deadline ordering, sacrificing faster service for high‑paying but low‑impact tickets. This may disappoint some enterprise customers but protects the platform and most users.
hardest_call: Placing the security incident (TICK-00771) before the overdue export failure (TICK-00982) was the tightest decision; one could argue the overdue bug affects more users and should be first, while the breach could have hidden consequences.

which_way_it_leaned_towards.why: Damage ranking best reflects the real harm to customers and the platform, aligning with our policy to protect those most affected.

rejected.money: Leading with money would have pushed high‑paying but low‑impact tickets ahead of critical incidents, ignoring real harm.
rejected.damage: We did not reject damage; it is our primary lens.
rejected.deadline: A pure deadline focus would have elevated the near‑deadline feature request over the security case, risking a breach.
rejected.fairness: Fairness would have placed the overdue export first but would have demoted the massive data loss, which is unacceptable.

which_way_it_leaned_towards.what_it_costs_us: Prioritising damage may delay responses for big‑paying customers with minor issues, potentially harming revenue or satisfaction.
